'''Andriy Oleksiyovych Lunin''' ({{langx|uk|Андрі́й Олексі́йович Лу́нін}}; born 11 February 1999) is a Ukrainian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Spanish football updater|Real Madrid}} club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and the [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine national team]].

Lunin began his senior career in Ukraine with [[FC Dnipro|Dnipro]] before joining [[FC Zorya Luhansk|Zorya Luhansk]]. He signed for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2018 and subsequently spent time on loan with [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], [[Real Valladolid]] and [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]]. After returning to Madrid, he served mainly as a backup to [[Thibaut Courtois]], but became the club's starting goalkeeper for much of the 2023–24 season following Courtois' injury. Lunin played a key role in Madrid's run to the [[2024 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]], as the club won [[La Liga]] and the [[UEFA Champions League]].

Lunin represented [[Ukraine national under-20 football team|Ukraine at youth level]] and was part of the team that won the [[2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup]]. He made his senior debut for the [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine national team]] in 2018 and later represented the country at major international tournaments.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Lunin was a player for Metalist Youth Sportive School (first trainer was Oleksandr Khrabrov) and Dnipro Youth Sportive School Systems (first trainer was Kostiantyn Pavliuchenko).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Matthew |date=8 July 2023 |title=Andriy Lunin Biography |url=https://footbalium.com/lifestyle/biography/19371-andriy-lunin-biography/ |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=Footbalium |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Dnipro===
[[File:Andriy Lunin.jpg|left|thumb|213x213px|Lunin with [[FC Dnipro|Dnipro]] in 2016]]
From summer 2016, after graduation of the youth sportive school, he played in the [[FC Dnipro-2 Dnipropetrovsk|Dnipro reserves]]. In the main-team squad, Lunin made his debut as a start-squad player at the age of 17, in the match against [[FC Karpaty Lviv|Karpaty Lviv]] on 16 October 2016 in the [[Ukrainian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=UPL Official Web Site|script-title=uk:Ліга Парі-Матч. 11 тур. Матч № 66 16 October 2016.|url=http://fpl.ua/ukr/protocol/2016_2017/pl/1/14/|language=uk|date=16 October 2016|access-date=16 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110063833/http://www.fpl.ua/ukr/protocol/2016_2017/pl/1/14|archive-date=10 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was Dnipro's first choice goalkeeper the rest of the season, playing in a total of 25 matches for the club, across the league and club competitions. However, at the end of the season, due to financial irregularities, Dnipro was relegated directly to the [[Ukrainian Second League]] (third level of football), and many players, Lunin included, were allowed to leave the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportarena.com/football/ukraina-pervaya-liga/ffu-skoro-reshit-kto-zajmet-mesto-dnepra-v-pervoj-lige/|title=ФФУ скоро решит, кто займет место Днепра в Первой лиге – Первая лига Украины|date=13 June 2017|website=SPORTARENA.com|language=ru|trans-title=FFU will soon decide who will take Dnipro's place in the First League|access-date=16 June 2019}}</ref>

===Zorya Luhansk===
Lunin spent the [[2017–18 Ukrainian Premier League|2017–18 season]] playing for [[FC Zorya Luhansk|Zorya Luhansk]], where he once again quickly established himself as the first keeper. On 14 September 2017, Lunin made his European debut in a 0–2 [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] group stage loss to [[Östersunds FK|Östersunds]] at the [[Arena Lviv]]. He ended up playing in 36 matches across all competitions that season, including all six of Zorya's Europa League matches.

===Real Madrid===
[[File:FC RB Salzburg gegen Real Madrid (Testspiel, 7. August 2019) 18.jpg|thumb|249x249px|Lunin training with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2019]]
On 19 June 2018, [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] reached an agreement with Zorya Luhansk to sign Lunin in a reportedly [[Euro|€]]8.5 million plus 5 million add-ons deal.<ref>[https://www.unian.info/m/society/10159028-real-madrid-sign-goalkeeper-andriy-lunin.html Real Madrid sign goalkeeper Andriy Lunin], [[UNIAN]] (20 June 2018)</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Andriy Lunin|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/06/official-announcement-andriy-lunin|publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]]|date=22 June 2018|access-date=22 June 2018}}</ref> On 27 August 2018, he was loaned to nearby fellow La Liga team [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], for the [[2018–19 La Liga|season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=El joven portero Andriy Lunin firma por el C.D. Leganés cedido por el Real Madrid|url=https://www.cdleganes.com/noticia/el-joven-portero-andriy-lunin-firma-por-el-c-d-leganes-cedido-por-el-real-madrid|publisher=CD Leganés|date=27 August 2018|access-date=27 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222182639/https://www.cdleganes.com/noticia/el-joven-portero-andriy-lunin-firma-por-el-c-d-leganes-cedido-por-el-real-madrid|archive-date=22 December 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Official Announcement: Lunin|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/official-announcement-lunin|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|date=27 August 2018|access-date=27 August 2018}}</ref> Halfway through the campaign, he stated that he was content with being second choice to [[Iván Cuéllar]], and would complete his contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=On loan Andriy Lunin opposed to January Bernabéu return |url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/12/31/football/1546248768_621194.html |access-date=1 July 2019 |work=Diario AS |date=31 December 2018}}</ref>

On 13 August 2019, he was loaned to [[Real Valladolid]] for the [[2019–20 La Liga|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=El Pucela obtiene la cesión de Lunin|url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticia/el-pucela-obtiene-la-cesion-de-lunin|access-date=13 August 2019|work=realvalladolid.es|date=13 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Lunin|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/08/official-announcement-lunin|access-date=13 August 2019|work=realmadrid.com|date=13 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813205344/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/08/official-announcement-lunin|archive-date=13 August 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 15 October 2019, Lunin was included in the 20 best under-21 players shortlist for the 2019 Golden Boy award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/golden-boy-2019-mason-mount-de-ligt-joao-felix-chelsea-guendouzi-arsenal-a9156361.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/golden-boy-2019-mason-mount-de-ligt-joao-felix-chelsea-guendouzi-arsenal-a9156361.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Golden Boy 2019: Mason Mount, Matthijs De Ligt and Joao Felix included in 20-man shortlist|last=Rathborn|first=Jack|date=15 October 2019|website=Independent|access-date=28 February 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

On 15 January 2020, the loan with Real Valladolid was terminated. On the same day, [[Real Oviedo]] announced the loan of Lunin until 30 June 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/15/official-announcement|title=Official Announcement|website=realmadrid.com|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/01/15/5e1ef78346163f0c7e8b4570.html|title=Real Madrid send Lunin to Oviedo|date=15 January 2020|website=Marca.com|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref>

On 20 January 2021, he made his first team debut for Real Madrid in a 1–2 extra time loss to [[CD Alcoyano|Alcoyano]] in the [[2020–21 Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55722360|title=Alcoyano 2–1 Real Madrid: Third division side cause huge upset|website=bbc.com|date=21 January 2021}}</ref> With Madrid confirmed [[2021–22 La Liga|2021–22]] champions, Lunin made his league debut on 8 May 2022 in the [[Madrid derby]] against [[Atlético Madrid]], which Real lost 1–0.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Atletico beat champions Real in Madrid derby |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61374121 |access-date=10 May 2022}}</ref> On 15 May 2022, he played against [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]], saving a penalty and allowing his team to draw 1–1 away from home.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lunin impresses for Real Madrid and exacts revenge against Sergio Gonzalez |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2022/05/16/6282029ee2704e1eac8b4589.html |website=www.marca.com |access-date=15 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cadiz 1–1 Real Madrid: Lunin show causes hosts to drop into relegation zone |url=https://english.stadiumastro.com/football/cadiz-11-real-madrid-lunin-show-causes-hosts-drop-relegation-zone-214683 |website=www.stadiumastro.com |date=15 May 2022 |access-date=15 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Brilló en Cádiz: Lunin estuvo exigido y detuvo hasta un penalti con un paradón |url=https://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/1652635205-brillo-en-cadiz-lunin-estuvo-exigido-y-detuvo-hasta-un-penalti-con-un-paradon |website=www.defensacentral.com |date=15 May 2022 |access-date=15 May 2022}}</ref>

On 5 October 2022, Lunin made his [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut in a 2–1 win against [[Shakhtar Donetsk]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.uaf.ua/article/46501 |title=Champions League. "Shakhtar" in Madrid conceded to "Real" Andriy Lunin |website=en.uaf.ua |date=5 October 2022 |access-date=16 October 2022 |archive-date=23 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230323053608/https://en.uaf.ua/article/46501 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 16 October 2022, he became the first Ukrainian player to feature in [[El Clásico]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], with Real winning 3–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2022-10-15-the-guy-has-my-full-trust-fans-speak-up-on-lunin-ahead-of-his-el-clasico-debut/ |title='The guy has my full trust' – fans speak up on Lunin ahead of his El Clasico debut |website=tribuna.com |date=15 October 2022 }}</ref>

On 8 November 2023, Lunin was called to action in Real Madrid's Champions League [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] match against [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] after [[Kepa Arrizabalaga|Kepa]] suffered an injury during the warm-up.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kallas |first=Fernando |date=8 November 2023 |title=Real Madrid beat Braga 3–0 to clinch Champions League last-16 place |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/real-madrid-beat-braga-3-0-clinch-champions-league-last-16-place-2023-11-08/ |access-date=9 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2023 |title=Real Madrid goalkeeper Kepa misses Champions League game after injury in warmups |url=https://apnews.com/article/real-madrid-kepa-lunin-braga-champions-league-67fffddcab6404402c766c1e5c34d68a |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> Lunin made a significant contribution to the team's performance by saving a penalty shot from Braga winger [[Álvaro Djaló]] in the fourth minute of the game, which helped maintain Real Madrid's lead in their group standings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guyett |first=Matthew |date=8 November 2023 |title="Clear of Kepa", "Best backup keeper in the world" – Fans react as Real Madrid keeper Andriy Lunin saves penalty in UCL fixture against Braga |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/news-clear-kepa-best-backup-keeper-world-fans-react-real-madrid-keeper-andriy-lunin-saves-penalty-ucl-fixture-braga |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=Sportskeeda |language=en-gb}}</ref>

On 13 February 2024, in a standout performance during Real Madrid's [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Champions League knockout stage match]] against [[RB Leipzig]] at the [[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|Red Bull Arena]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=13 February 2024 |title=Leipzig-Real Madrid: UEFA Champions League 2023/24 Round of 16 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2039914--leipzig-vs-real-madrid/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref> Lunin equaled [[Thibaut Courtois]]' [[2022 UEFA Champions League final]] record by making nine saves in a single match, which garnered significant acclaim from the manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 February 2024 |title=Ancelotti: "It was a tough, difficult game but the team dug in until the end" |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/press-conference/ancelotti-13-02-2024 |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=Real Madrid CF |language=en-US}}</ref> Ancelotti hailed it as Lunin's "best game" for the club, emphasising the goalkeeper's critical role in securing a strong position for Real Madrid to advance in the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dempsey |first=Ethan |date=13 February 2024 |title=Carlo Ancelotti lauds keeper Lunin for his 'best game' in the win against Leipzig |url=https://footbalium.com/champions-league/68587-carlo-ancelotti-lauds-keeper-lunin-for-his-best-game-against-leipzig/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=Footbalium |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 17 April 2024, Lunin made eight saves in the Champions League quarter-finals' second leg against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], which ended in a 1–1 draw, and then went on to stop Manchester City players [[Bernardo Silva]] and [[Mateo Kovačić]]'s penalties in the shootout, securing Real Madrid's advancement to the semi-finals.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 April 2024 |title=Lunin the hero as Real Madrid eliminate Manchester City on penalties |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/champions-league/2024/04/17/66201e0d268e3e511e8b45ad.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502041412/https://www.marca.com/en/football/champions-league/2024/04/17/66201e0d268e3e511e8b45ad.html |archive-date=2 May 2024 |access-date=18 April 2024 |publisher=MARCA |language=en }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=17 April 2024 |title=Manchester City 1–1 Real Madrid (agg: 4–4 aet, 3–4 pens): Real Madrid hold nerve in shoot-out |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/028c-1aad6a5c7b4a-4c4a76ccd847-1000--manchester-city-1-1-real-madrid-agg-4-4-aet-3-4-pens-real-/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501080506/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/028c-1aad6a5c7b4a-4c4a76ccd847-1000--manchester-city-1-1-real-madrid-agg-4-4-aet-3-4-pens-real-/ |archive-date=1 May 2024 |access-date=18 April 2024 |publisher=UEFA |language=en }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 April 2024 |title=Real Madrid exact revenge on Man City to reach Champions League semis |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240417-real-madrid-exact-revenge-on-man-city-to-reach-champions-league-semis |access-date=17 April 2024 |website=France 24 |language=en}}</ref> 

On 13 September 2024, Lunin extended his contract, signing a new five-year deal to remain at Madrid until 2030.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 September 2024 |title=Official Announcement: Andriy Lunin contract renewal |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-renovacion-lunin-13-09-2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913183831/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-renovacion-lunin-13-09-2024 |archive-date=13 September 2024 |access-date=13 September 2024 |publisher=Real Madrid CF |language=en }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Андрей Лунин. 12 октября 2018 года — 915374 (cropped).jpg|thumb|224x224px|Lunin with [[Ukraine national under-21 football team|Ukraine U21]] in 2018]]
In 2019, Lunin backstopped [[Ukraine national under-20 football team|Ukraine U20]] team to their first ever [[2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup|FIFA U-20 World Cup]] victory.<ref name=":0"/> He played in six of his team's seven matches, but missed the quarterfinal match against [[Colombia national under-20 football team|Colombia]] due to being called up to Ukraine's main squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] matches against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] and [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]].<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=uk:Лунин попрощался с молодежной сборной и отправился в национальную|trans-title=Lunin said goodbye to the junior team and went to the national team|url=https://euro2020.football.ua/news/article/392883-lunin-poproshhalsja-s-molodezhnojj-sbornojj-i-otpravilsja-v-nacionalnuju.html|website=football.ua|access-date=16 June 2019|language=uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://football.ua/countrieselse/393528-lunin-vernulsja-v-raspolozhenie-molodezhnojj-sbornojj-ukrainy.html|script-title=uk:Лунин вернулся в расположение молодежной сборной Украины|trans-title=Lunin is back with Ukraine's junior team|website=football.ua|access-date=16 June 2019|language=uk}}</ref> After the 3–1 final match victory against [[South Korea national under-20 football team|South Korea]], Lunin was awarded the Golden Glove as the best goalkeeper of the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/news/lee-lunin-headline-award-winners-at-poland-2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190616014756/https://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/news/lee-lunin-headline-award-winners-at-poland-2019|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 June 2019|title=Lee, Lunin headline award winners at Poland 2019|website=[[FIFA]]|access-date=16 June 2019}}</ref>

On 23 March 2018, Lunin debuted for the [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine national team]] in a 1–1 [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] draw against [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]].<ref name="apostrophe.ua">{{Cite news|script-title=uk:Голкіпер "Зорі" встановив рекорд збірної України|trans-title=Zorya goalkeeper set a record for the Ukraine national football team|url=https://apostrophe.ua/ua/news/sport/2018-03-24/golkiper-zari-ustanovil-rekord-sbornoy-ukrainyi-/125149|website=apostrophe.ua|date=24 March 2018|access-date=23 June 2024|language=uk}}</ref> At the age of 19 years and 40 days, he became the youngest debutant in the national team during that time, surpassing the previous records set by [[Maksym Koval (footballer)|Maksym Koval]] and [[Oleksandr Shovkovskyi]].<ref name="apostrophe.ua"/>

In May 2024, Lunin was called up to represent Ukraine at [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{cite news |date=16 May 2024|script-title=uk:Сергій Ребров оголосив склад національної команди України на підготовчий збір і товариські матчі перед Євро-2024 |trans-title=Serhii Rebrov announces the squad of the national team of Ukraine for the preparatory training camp and friendly matches before Euro 2024 |url=https://uaf.ua/article/51338 |language=uk |publisher=[[Ukrainian Association of Football|Ukrainian Football Association]] |access-date=30 May 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Lunin married his girlfriend Anastasia Tomazova in a civil ceremony in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 March 2021 |title=Andriy Lunin gets married... In a tracksuit! |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/03/19/6054da71e2704e7a858b4610.html |access-date=1 May 2026 |website=MARCA |language=en}}</ref>
